# LG AI Research & KAIST at EHRSQL 2024: Self-Training Large Language Models with Pseudo-Labeled Unanswerable Questions for a Reliable Text-to-SQL System on EHRs

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#pluq)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-18**

[Original source](https://aclanthology.org/2024.clinicalnlp-1.61.pdf) · ClinicalNLP 2024 proceedings, pp. 635–643; nine-page paper

**Reading coverage:** All nine PDF pages: Sections 1–5, limitations, acknowledgments, references, three figures and four tables. The training diagram, score definition, prompt and all results/ablation tables were visually checked on PDF pages 3 and 5–7. No appendix is present. Author publication listing inspected separately; no private repository was accessed.

## Research question

Clinical SQL systems need to withhold unsupported or unreliable predictions despite class imbalance between answerable and unanswerable requests.

## Method

Fine-tunes GPT-3.5-Turbo-0125 on labeled EHRSQL data and schema/instruction prompts. The seed labels development/test questions, and predicted-unanswerable examples augment another training round. Maximum token entropy and execution-error/empty-result filters then replace uncertain outputs with a null refusal.

## Evaluation

The EHRSQL 2024 shared-task development/test setting uses a MIMIC-IV demo database and penalty-based reliability scores. Model, prompt and filter ablations are reported on development data; the test question pool participates in pseudo-label training without access to its gold answers.

## What the results support

Table 1 reports test RS(10) of 81.32 and RS(N) of -711.83. In Table 4, adding entropy filtering raises development RS(10) from 85.38 to 88.65 while lowering RS(0) from 93.98 to 90.37. The trade-off depends on error penalties rather than improving every outcome.

## Limits and qualifications

This is transductive adaptation, not a clean unseen-question test. Seed-generated labels are not independently validated; filter thresholds use an assumed unanswerable proportion. Execution failures or empty/None results do not prove intrinsic unanswerability. The ablations do not isolate self-training with all other components fixed. Training-count wording is inconsistent, and Table 1 qualifies its development result as not posted to the leaderboard. No clinical deployment is evaluated.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

A directly relevant unanswerability/self-training baseline with explicit distinctions between unsupported requests, uncertain SQL, evaluation-pool adaptation and penalty-dependent abstention.
